newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds recovered from their worst intraday levels but still ended sharply weaker on Wednesday on the back of selling from all quarters on the local front, bond traders said.
At 1420 GMT government's benchmark R150 stock was yielding 14.92 percent from 14.825 percent late on Tuesday and after touching the day's weakest level of 14.96 percent.

"The market weakened sharply over lunch-time, breaking key technical levels (around 14.85 percent) on the way up. There was selling from all quarters at home...institutions and others," a trader said.
He said the yield on the R150 climbed to 14.96 percent before it hit a top and profit-taking set in.
The late afternoon then saw a spate of institutional buying as players saw good value at the higher level.
Traders said the overall trend in the market was negative.

"The main issue is that there is a lack of demand after offshore players initially bought bonds last week following the many new Eurorand issues announced in the longer end of the market," one trader pointed out.
New Eurorand issues announced this week had little impact as they were mainly in the short-end of the market.
Bonds were seen holding a 14.88 to 15.00 percent range on Thursday.
The Bond Market Exchange said foreigners were net sellers of 185.34 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 1.052 billion rand's worth on Mnnday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 6.39 billion rand from 4.92 billion rand previously.
On the forex side, the rand wa3 little changed from its previous closing levels after two-way exporter/importer trade.
"It was a fairly steady day but the bond market put pressure one the rand," a forex dealer noted.
He said importer demand took the local unit higher to the 4.46 level on the top where it was met by export orders which capped further weakness.
"There's pressure on the 4.46 level which was tried and taken down several times today," the trader said.
Thursday's direction was seen dicated by the bond market.

The rand continued weak but off its lows against sterling after cable was boosted this week following a hike in interest rates in the U.K on Tuesday and moves to increase the Bank of England's independence.
Against the pound the rand was last at 7.2872/2966 from 7.2882/2975 on Tuesday. It slid to a two-month low against sterling on Tuesday when it touched a 7.3039 bid.
Against the other crosses, the rand was last at 0.3861/3866 on the mark from 0.3869/3872 on Tuesday, and at 28.0570/0871 yen from 28.1611/2025 yen previously.
On the money market major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 9.502 billion on Tuesday from 10.256 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
